ядра.ядро_en: Provide an image and use text prompts to add, remove, or modify elements, change the style, or adjust the color grading.

модели_различия.текст_en: 2.5 Flash Image blog (adjust colors); recipes; Gemini app
Gemini API docs

оговорки.текст_en: 'Image + text-to-image (editing): Provide an image and use text prompts to add, remove, or modify elements, change the style, or adjust colors.'
'You can add, remove, or change objects and backgrounds.'
Input can be text, images, video, or a combination, which lets you 'create, edit, and iterate on visuals'.
Mechanism: native multimodality — 'the model can understand and incorporate an existing image into its creative process'; 'Edit images with simple, natural language instructions.'
Gemini app wording: 'telling Gemini to change the background, replace an object, or add an element – all while preserving the details you love.'

Product pages restate the operations: 'Add anything to a selfie with Gemini.'; Slides: 'enhance or add custom, relevant elements into any image'; 'adding background, text, or resizing images' (Nano Banana Pro).

приёмы.текст_en: 'Provide an image and simply describe the change you want.' / 'Just give Gemini a photo to work with, and tell it what you'd like to change.'

Add — official examples name the object with attributes and mostly where it goes: 'Add a fluffy white cat.', 'Now, add a stack of three books to the coffee table.', 'add more palm trees in the background', 'Please add a red bow tie and a black top hat to the person in the image.'; the cookbook adds a fallback: 'Add a blue planet on the figurine's helmet or hat (add one if needed)'.
Remove: 'Remove the man from the photo', 'erase the fence', 'Remove the reflection on the window.', 'remove the pancakes and add an omelet'.
Change an attribute: 'Change the sofa's color to a deep navy blue.', 'make the sunglasses red', 'Now change the color to yellow.', 'Make the lighting darker.'
Replace: 'Swap the arrow pointing up in the picture for a red arrow pointing down', 'Replace volumetric lighting with bokeh', 'Replace the roof with thatch and add bamboo structural elements.'
Background: 'Change the background to the corporate colors: blue and white.', 'Change the background to an elegant ballroom setting with chandeliers and ornate decorations.'

Chain on the Gemini tips page: a base prompt that names the objects ('A high-quality photo of a modern, minimalist living room with a grey sofa, a light wood coffee table, and a large potted plant.'), then one edit per follow-up addressing them ('Change the sofa's color to a deep navy blue.', 'Now, add a stack of three books to the coffee table.').

ядра.ситуация_в_промпте: There is a finished image to change with words; the first question is what can be asked at all; The task is to add, remove, recolor or replace a specific item or the background in a finished image.
ядра.не_применяется_когда: There is no input image; Changing the style of the whole image; assembling from several uploaded images (reference roles); translating captions (covered by the core on translating text in images).
ядра.магнит_причина: Concrete objects from Google's examples to generalize into a class: a fluffy white cat, a stack of three books, palm trees, a red bow tie and a black top hat.

оговорки.текст_en: The order of parts is not prescribed: Agent Platform samples put the image first in Python/Java/Node.js and the text first in Go; the Gemini API page and the hackathon JS guide put the text part first; the developers codelab uses contents=[prompt, image].
Images can be sent as base64 inline data with a mime type (e.g. image/png).
The Lite notebook passes Part.from_bytes(image, mime_type='image/png') before the text.
Firebase model comparison marks both 'Generate images' and 'Edit images' for all three Gemini 3.x image models.
Imagen (generate) can generate but not edit; Imagen (capability) can both generate and edit (Firebase, previous models).
Firebase migration table maps imagen-3.0-capability-001 → gemini-3.1-flash-image.

Veo 3 + Nano Banana quickstart: 'Edit Image: Edit an image based on a text prompt using Gemini 2.5 Flash Image'; 'Compose Image: Combine multiple images with a text prompt to create a new image'; [derived] Imagen 4 is used there only for text-to-image.
Vertex AI get-started: 'Gemini can generate and process images conversationally.' — prompt with text, images, or both for tasks such as image generation and editing.
A Gemini Image model can generate and edit images using both text-only and text-and-file prompts; you can ask a Gemini Image model to edit images by prompting with text and one or more images.

ядра.ядро_en: Editing requires a different mindset than generating. You already have a base image; your prompt needs to focus on what is changing and what is staying the same. Be explicit about what to keep exactly the same.

части.текст_en: Editing requires a different mindset than generating. You already have a base image; your prompt needs to focus on what is changing and what is staying the same.
Prompting tip: Be explicit about what to keep exactly the same.

модели_различия.текст_en: the tip is given in the guide for NB2/Pro; Pro examples carry preservation clauses
the tip is given in the guide for NB2/Pro
examples from the hackathon and the restoration notebook
all Gemini API docs templates contain a preservation clause
guide rule + examples with an invariant (pages 260/273) and without one (pages 260/263)
guide rule on page 317 + cookbook example with 'keeping everything else the same'
only a general Firebase example for all models
example 'Maintain existing pose and framing'; examples on page 304 without an invariant

оговорки.текст_en: In the source, the 'Be explicit about what to keep exactly the same' tip sits under semantic masking (inpainting).

On the Gemini API page every editing template and edit example pairs the change with a preservation clause: 'Keep everything else in the image exactly the same', 'Preserve the original composition', 'remain completely unchanged', 'Do not change any other elements of the image', 'Keep everything the same, but...'.
Hackathon JS guide examples: 'Leave the background unchanged.', 'leave everything else the same.'
Nano Banana Pro examples: 'while keeping everything else the same', 'keep the can exactly the same', 'remains exactly locked in its current position', 'retain his original features and expression'.
All editing templates on the 2.5 Flash Image blog reference the input and most state what must be preserved (everything else, original style, lighting, composition).

Fidelity-oriented restoration prompts add 'while preserving every original detail' / 'maintaining all original details without any additions'; creative transformations (watercolor, cinematization) on the same page do not.
Both positive ('Keep everything else ... exactly the same') and negative ('Do not change any other elements of the image.') clause forms appear in official prompts.

Official examples word the keep-clause in several ways: 'while keeping everything else the same' (Nano Banana Pro launch and tips pages), 'keeping everything else the same' (NB2 cookbook), 'The character, remains exactly locked in its current position', 'The man should retain his original features and expression' (Pro launch page), 'Maintain existing pose and framing' (Nano Banana Halloween post).
Firebase's in-image language example uses a negative keep-clause: 'Update this infographic to be in Spanish. Do not change any other elements of the image.'

Many official edit examples carry no keep-clause and name only the change: 'Remove the man from the photo' (the same guide's semantic-masking example), 'Turn this scene into nighttime', 'Focus on the flowers', 'Translate to French', 'Replace volumetric lighting with bokeh', 'Change the sofa's color to a deep navy blue.'

[derived by extractor] On the Nano Banana Pro launch page the change + invariant pairing appears in 4 of 16 prompts and the shortest edits carry none; on the Pro developers page edit prompts are 3-5 word commands naming only the change; on the Halloween post only the Victorian-ghost prompt has a preservation clause and none asks to keep the face unchanged.

приёмы.текст_en: Lead with the preservation, then the one change: 'Keep everything the same, but change the character's expression to be more serious.'
When replacing something, name what to carry over from the original: '...but with the same colors and patterns from my clothes and boots.'
Scope the preservation to what is at risk: 'Translate text to Spanish, keep the same text style.' / 'Keep his face the same.'

ядра.ядро_en: Editing Instructions: For modifying an existing image, be direct and specific (e.g., change the man's tie to green, remove the car in the background).

модели_различия.текст_en: NB Pro tips blog; command examples of 3-5 words
Google Earth examples: a single imperative sentence
NB tips blog: use natural language; the only literal prompt is a description of the end state
Agent Platform REST example (model in ${API_ENDPOINT})

оговорки.текст_en: 'Use natural language to replace an object, adjust placements or fix a sign to say something different.'

Edit prompts applied to an existing image on the Pro developer page are 3–5-word imperative commands (verb + target) that rely on the image for all other context: 'Replace volumetric lighting with bokeh', 'Translate to French'.
Gemini app examples open with an imperative transformation verb aimed at the input and add separate sentences for specifics.
Google Earth examples are single imperative sentences starting with an action verb; the on-screen view supplies the place.
Agent Platform examples reference the attached image ('this image', 'this photo') and state only the target change with an imperative verb, without re-describing the scene.
The only literal prompt on the Nano Banana tips page is a one-line description of the desired end state: 'the dog’s mouth is closed.'
On both Gemini-app prompting-tips pages this is the sixth prompt element and applies only 'For modifying an existing image'.
Some official examples do not say where: the Docs example 'Add a fluffy white cat.' names no place in the image.

приёмы.текст_en: Describe the change itself: 'Enter a prompt that describes how to adjust the image.' / 'In the bottom bar, describe how you want to change the image' (Docs); 'Upload an image and provide instructions to modify it' (Gemini 2.0 Flash quickstart); 'snap a picture and describe the edits you're looking for' (Lens).
'By using direct, conversational commands, you can modify specific elements within the image without needing complex software or re-generating the entire scene.'

ядра.ядро_en: An image editing prompt is based on natural language, typically using imperative or declarative instructions. With an imperative prompt, you describe the actions to perform on the input, while with a declarative prompt, you describe the expected output. Both are possible and will provide equivalent results.

модели_различия.текст_en: consistent-scenes notebook: imperative re-composition
restoration examples (imperative, description, key-value)
object detection/editing notebook and codelab

оговорки.текст_en: 'When several geometric transformations are involved, it can be challenging to craft an imperative prompt that details all the operations to perform. Instead, a descriptive prompt can be more straightforward by directly describing the expected output' — e.g. requesting an 'upright' visual 'filling the canvas'.
'This imperative prompt composes the scene in terms of actions. It's sometimes easier than writing descriptions.'
A third form shown is a key-value prompt: Task / Subject / Corrections / Background / Border / Position.
The codelab names the two styles 'imperative' and 'descriptive'.

приёмы.текст_en: 'If you have complex transformations, craft your prompts iteratively, going from the most difficult operation to the last details.'

примеры.текст:
- Isolate and straighten the visual on a pure white background, excluding any surrounding text.
- Clean up all physical artifacts and noise while preserving every original detail.
- Center the result and scale it to fit the canvas with minimal, symmetrical margins, ensuring no distortion or cropping.

ядра.ядро_en: Edit prompts refer to the input explicitly — by content ('Using the provided image of [subject]', 'Transform the provided photograph of [subject]'), by order or role ('the first image', 'the second image', 'the provided source image'), or deictically ('this image', 'these ingredients', 'that cat', 'it') — and multi-turn edits carry the reference instead of re-describing or re-uploading.

recipes: ordinal references following the order of parts; blog templates refer to the input
cookbook: deictic words + previous_interaction_id

оговорки.текст_en: In the recipes notebook, ordinal references follow the order of parts in the request ([model_image, garment_image, text] -> 'the person in the first image', 'the garment from the second image').

All editing templates on the 2.5 Flash Image blog explicitly reference the input ('Using the provided image...', 'Transform the provided photograph...', 'combining the elements from the provided images').

приёмы.текст_en: Label personal inputs in the first sentence: 'This is a photo of me and my dog.' / 'This is a photo of my younger self and a photo of myself today.' / 'Here’s a picture of me as an adult.'
List the inputs by index before the instructions: '- Image 1: Reference robot character sheet. - Image 2: Previous scene.'
Refer to the uploaded photo by what it shows ('my cat') rather than 'this image'.
In follow-ups, reuse the noun from the earlier prompt ('the tree', 'the poppies', 'the perfume bottle').

ядра.ядро_en: Official edit prompts are short imperative instructions aimed at the input that describe only the change: a transformation or edit verb (Create / Restore / Turn / Transform / Recreate / Place / Add / Change) with a reference to the input ('this photo', 'this image', 'this product', 'these ingredients', 'that figurine') and the target ('Turn this photo into...', 'Recreate this cat as...', 'Transform this house into...'), then separate sentences with specifics ('Include...', 'Plate it as if...', 'Replace...', 'Surround it with...', 'Do not include...'); they do not re-describe the source image, and several follow-ups start with 'Now,'.

оговорки.текст_en: 'break down a complex task into smaller steps, like decorating an empty room one piece of furniture at a time' — possible because the model 'doesn't treat each new request as a blank slate' and understands what it just created.

Gemini app: 'take an empty room, paint the walls, then add a bookshelf, some furniture or a coffee table. Gemini's working with you all along to alter specific parts of an image while preserving the rest.'
The model can also 'follow complex editing instructions in a single step', and official chat turns often bundle two or three edits in one message.
Cookbook and Lite notebook follow-ups refer back with deictic words or the same nouns ('that cat', 'that figurine', 'it', 'the tree') and make one main change per turn.
Agent Platform names 'iteratively work on an image' among the recommended tasks for Gemini Image.
Positioned workflows: iterative refinement and context-aware conversational editing; 'edit images until they’re just right'.
Gemini 2.0 Flash: 'Collaboratively edit images in real-time.'
'given the non-deterministic nature of large language models it might take a few tries for you to get a good result.'

Kaggle hackathon insight (Google DeepMind host): projects used 'the previous generated image as a critical input for the next generation', enabling conversational editing (e.g., 'Make it sunset,' 'Move object closer') 'that preserves original image DNA'.

Products: 'With new multi-turn prompting, you can refine your visuals iteratively' (Vids, Pro); 'Use follow-ups to keep editing' (Lens); Volley's game makes 'quick iterative edits from chat or voice' (2.5 Flash Image).
[derived by extractor] Vids avatars follow create-then-refine with specific tweak requests; follow-up examples refer to the prior output by deixis and one edit is one sentence.
On the same Gemini API page Nano Banana 2 Lite is 'Not optimized for multiple reference inputs or multi-turn sequential editing.'

приёмы.текст_en: Refinement follow-up that locks everything and changes one thing: 'Keep everything the same, but change the character's expression to be more serious.'
'start with a base image and issue follow-up commands to change specific details—like colors or objects—without needing to rewrite the entire prompt from scratch' (Nano Banana Pro lab).
'If the result isn't quite right, you can simply tell Gemini what was incorrect and try again.' / 'If you don't like what you see, just ask Gemini to change it.'
Firebase chain changes one thing per turn: '[image of a blue car] + Turn this car into a convertible.', then 'Now change the color to yellow.'
Follow-ups refer to the subject from context: 'Add a blue planet on the figurine's helmet or hat (add one if needed)', then 'Move that figurine to a tropical beach'.

оговорки.текст_en: Nano Banana Pro: 'Select, refine and transform any part of an image with improved localized editing.'
Google calls this 'pixel-perfect editing': change a single detail — for example, the color of a sofa — without disturbing the rest of the scene.
'alter parts of an image while keeping the rest the same ... all while preserving important details of the original'; 'edit only one part of an image while leaving the rest completely untouched'.
Gemini 2.0 Flash (preview): 'Edit specific parts of images conversationally, without changing anything else.'
The mask is expressed in words, not as a mask image; Agent Platform describes Gemini Image as offering 'mask-free editing'.
'masked editing' is named among advanced features under Limitations that may sometimes produce unnatural results.
Prompting tip in the same section: be explicit about what to keep exactly the same.
Gemini app multi-turn editing: Gemini alters specific parts of an image while preserving the rest.

No drawn mask is used on the Gemini path: the Android developers blog sends the photo plus the text 'remove the pancakes and add an omelet' in a chat, while the same task with Imagen takes a mask image (see the linked Imagen mask-inpainting core).
Model cards list 'Masked/Doodle based editing: partial instruction following and persistent ink' as a known limitation (see the linked model-card limitation core).
Google names 'local edits in an infinite canvas' among the community uses of Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image).
Pro wording: 'Select, refine and transform any part of an image with improved localized editing.'

приёмы.текст_en: Name the part to change in words. Google's own lists of local edits: 'blur the background of an image, remove a stain in a t-shirt, remove an entire person from a photo, alter a subject's pose, add color to a black and white photo' (2.5 Flash Image); 'From removing a person from a group photo to fixing a small detail like a stain' (Vertex AI blog).

примеры.текст: Remove the man from the photo
примеры.что_показывает_en: Semantic-mask edit: the object to remove is named in words.

примеры.текст: text("remove the pancakes and add an omelet")
примеры.что_показывает_en: Region edit expressed in words and sent with the photo in a chat (Android developers blog).

ядра.ситуация_в_промпте: The edit concerns one place in the image (an item, area or detail), the rest must not move, and there is no way to draw a mask; One part of a finished image has to change (an item, the background, a stain, a person) while the rest stays; the area can only be 'selected' with words.
ядра.не_применяется_когда: Working with Imagen and a pixel mask area (mask-based editing) is a different model and mechanism; A full redraw or restyle; an Imagen call with a mask image (there the mask is a separate input); products that let you draw on the image (Gemini app, Pics).
ядра.магнит_причина: Google's lists of local edits in the techniques name concrete objects (a stain in a t-shirt, an entire person removed from a photo, the pancakes swapped for an omelet) that a generator may copy.

противоречия.суть: Есть ли у Gemini-моделей правка по маске-области, которую задаёт пользователь (E-111-4 без разделения по моделям)

версии.текст: 'With Gemini and Imagen, you can ... Edit or expand an uploaded or generated image using a mask area you define.' (без разделения по моделям) (E-111-4; ранг 1)
'With Imagen on Agent Platform, you can ... edit only parts of images using a mask area you define' (E-49-23); mask-based editing — метод Imagen (E-129-3, E-129-5)
Gemini Image: '... mask-free editing. Uniquely capable of multi-turn conversational editing.' (E-111-17); маска задаётся словами (E-1-122)

противоречия.решение: Разнесено по моделям: маска-область, которую задаёт пользователь, — функция Imagen (E-49-23, E-129-3, E-129-5); Gemini Image — без маски, область называют словами (E-111-17, E-1-122). Imagen снят (E-228-3, E-228-4, E-1-177).

противоречия.суть: Что значит «masked editing» / «Masked/Doodle based editing» в Limitations и карточках Pro, NB2, Lite

версии.текст: 'Advanced features like masked editing … may sometimes produce unnatural results' (Limitations страниц Pro и NB2)
'Masked/Doodle based editing: partial instruction following and persistent ink' (карточка Pro)
'Conversationally define a "mask"' — маска словами (доки Gemini API)

противоречия.решение: Не решено: страницы не говорят, пиксельная это маска, рисунок на самой картинке или маска словами (реестр С-19); closes by: живой замер.

связи.пояснение: карточки 3.x: «Masked/Doodle based editing» — известное ограничение (данные ч2 к спору)

ядра.примечание: данные ч2 к спору: карточки 3.x называют «Masked/Doodle based editing: partial instruction following and persistent ink» известным ограничением (Я-редактирование-31); маска-картинка (maskImage) в API есть только у Imagen (Я-редактирование-30); в продуктах область обводят рисунком (Я-редактирование-72). Правилами (а)–(ж) спор не решён (версии не о разных моделях, даты — штампы Last updated или нет), статус «спор» оставлен; closes by: живой замер (С-19: работает ли маска, нарисованная на входной картинке); Л3: Imagen-часть историческая (снят 2026-08-17), ядро держится частью о Gemini

ядра.подтема: Imagen: маска-инпейнтинг и аутпейнтинг (отдельный путь)
ядра.ядро_en: You can now draw a mask and utilize inpainting to generate pixels within the masked area. Additionally, outpainting is available to generate pixels outside the mask. You provide both a sourceImage, a maskImage and a prompt for the edit and the number of edit steps to be performed.

части.текст_en: Mask-based inpainting / outpainting: 'modify specific areas of an image without regenerating the entire picture'; changes are made 'modifying only the area in the mask'.

ядра.ядро_en: Upload an image of your space, and watch the app generate a variety of fully realized concepts, from Mid-Century Modern to Bohemian Chic.

оговорки.текст_en: Space Lift is 'a demo interior design app powered by Nano Banana 2 Lite and Gemini Omni'; it 'automatically generates fully realized concepts across various design aesthetics'.
The Lens demo is a description, not a verbatim prompt: the user 'asks to see it reimagined using the "dopamine decor" trend'.
Related uses: Messages Remix names 'redesigning rooms'; Android page: 'alter the background of a room to sample new wallpaper'.

приёмы.текст_en: Describe decorating ideas on your own photo: 'Snap a photo of your front porch or living room, describe different decorating ideas and generate images with Nano Banana to see how they look.'
Ask and request the updated image in one turn: '[image of a furnished room] + What other color sofas would work in my space? Can you update the image?'

Exterior remodel, general theme then concrete replacements then surroundings: 'Transform this house into a vibrant tropical island design. Replace the roof with thatch and add bamboo structural elements. Surround it with lush, colorful tropical plants and palm trees.'

[image of a furnished room] +
What other color sofas would work in my space? Can you update the image?

оговорки.текст_en: By the page's alt texts, 'Take this concept and localize it to a setting in Germany, including translation' also replaced scene elements (e.g. a bus with a tram, the menu), not only the text.

Two different operations, not a model difference: plain translation keeps the original style and layout (Pro: E-137-14), while localizing a concept 'to a [country] setting' also changes the visuals (Pro: E-135-25; NB2 ad localizer: E-148-9); the wording of the prompt decides.

State the translation scope explicitly: 'Take this concept and localize it to an Indian setting, including translation of all the text to Hindi.'
Name a key phrase to translate faithfully: '...making sure to translate the words "Taste the Aura" accurately and authentically'.

---
name: paintings
description: Restoration protocol for fine art paintings.
---

# Painting restoration

Perform direct, minimal-intervention restoration of fine art paintings. Prioritize historical integrity, original pigment depth, and surface textures over cosmetic modernization. Do not include any elements, nor introduce any techniques not present in the original piece.

### 1. Core conservation mandates
* **Absolute Fidelity:** Strictly forbidden to add new subjects, figures, scenery, details, or narrative elements under any circumstances.
* **Anti-Modernization:** Retain original brushstroke characteristics. Do not flatten support textures.
* **Patina & Craquelure:** Respect the natural crack network (craquelure) as part of the artwork's history. Do not fill or erase cracks unless they pose an active risk of paint loss.

### 2. Step-by-step restoration process
1. **Varnish Correction:** Gently balance aged, yellowed natural varnishes to recover original pigment chromaticity without forcing modern, high-contrast saturation.
2. **Soot & Grime Reduction:** Isolate and lift surface grime while protecting delicate, thin underlying glaze layers.
3. **Inpaint Major Loss:** Where paint layers are missing, use references from the surviving elements to bridge the gap. Replicate the original brush direction, speed, height, transparency, and light source.

Workspace Experiments help: 'You can ask Gemini to edit your images or infographics.' Click on an image and select the icon at its bottom-left corner → 'In the bottom bar, describe how you want to change the image' (or pick a suggestion: More → prompt starter) → send → Accept to insert the edits.

сводка: Шаг правки (4б): 87 ядер сшивки → 85. По Л2 убраны в не_сведено как примеры правил: Я-редактирование-11 (в 10), 18 (в 14, Л13: лицо при правке), 23 (в 22, слито по Б-51); размердж по Л9: смена ракурса (бывшее 1-30) отделена из составного 41 в новое Я-редактирование-88. Модели по Л1: 38 ячеек «да» → «не_сказано» (коды другой функции, строки ограничений карточек, выведенные единицы, модель по умолчанию в ноутбуке), 2 «да» добавлены при слиянии (14, 22 — pro), у 53 other = частично; Lite и многоходовая правка — оговорки E-1-13 (3: частично, 25: нет), спор С-15 открыт. Imagen (Л3): действует=false у 16 и 30; у 29 Imagen-часть помечена исторической, спор сужен до смысла «masked editing» (E-111-4 решена по (а)). Магниты (Л7): сняты флаги по служебным словам и у справочных ядер (54, 65, 68, 78, 79), поставлены по перечням артефактов и конкретным предметам примеров (16, 20, 31, 32, 35, 37, 41, 48, 50, 70, 76, 80–83, 88), причины переписаны. Склеены задвоенные оговорки и приёмы из копий страниц (32, 34, 41, 42, 48, 60); исправлены роли и лучшие источники (6, 26, 61, 62, 71, 72, 83); ранг стр. 243 → 3 (Б-100). Добавлены поля слой (промпт 47, инструкция 14, справка 24) и дом (24 ядра с домом в другой теме, связи «уточняет» на домашние ядра). Сомнения: Я-редактирование-29 оставлено действующим вопреки букве Л3; статусы «согласовано» при одной формулирующей странице и подтверждениях в оговорках не трогались, кроме ядер целиком на одной странице (58, 85, 86, 87).

Ядро темы — три шаблона правки Google дословно (add/remove/modify, change only … keep everything else, style transfer) плюс шаблон сохранения критичных деталей; они согласованы между доками (2026-09) и блогом 2.5 Flash Image (2025-08). Разведено «что модель делает сама» (подгоняет стиль, свет и перспективу; держит сходство; распознаёт артефакты при реставрации) и «что просить» (оговорка встраивания, оговорка сохранения, подробное описание лица/логотипа). Противоречий 6: 3 по (д) гайд-против-примера (совет про оговорку сохранения против примеров без неё; запретительные оговорки «Do not change…» против совета позитивной формы из темы «промптинг» — в Я-редактирование-1-7 и Я-редактирование-1-31), 1 по (е) текст-против-кода (пример add), 1 по (а) модель (перевод против локализации визуала), 1 спор (маска у Gemini: mask-free против masked editing в Limitations). Ограничения Pro/NB2 (masked editing, смена света день→ночь, смешение картинок) показаны теми же страницами как возможности — витрина не гарантия.
